# Frozen solar reference

`usno-baltimore-2026-09-29.json` is the unmodified JSON response retrieved on 2026-10-03 from the U.S. Naval Observatory Astronomical Applications API v4.0.1:

https://aa.usno.navy.mil/api/rstt/oneday?date=2026-09-29&coords=39.28%2C-76.61&tz=-4

API parameter documentation: https://aa.usno.navy.mil/data/api

The coordinates are latitude 39.28° N, longitude 76.61° W (Baltimore Inner Harbor vicinity). The requested date is 2026-09-29. The explicit offset is UTC−04:00 and the API's additional US daylight-saving adjustment is off (`isdst: false`), so 18:52 corresponds to 22:52 UTC. There is no station identifier or rolling bulletin version.

SHA-256 of the saved response bytes:
`950960fc7ee97b7c4b469d9629fb694558d1b39b29a4df6849beb2ddefd1f9d9`

The offline test reads this committed fixture and compares its sunset with the production sea-level Maghrib estimate, allowing two minutes for the approximate solar coordinates and rounded horizon/refraction convention. The fixture is an independently retrieved reference value, not a value generated by the extension. Tests and the installed extension make no reference lookup. This only validates sunset for this case; it does not validate all prayer conventions, every location or OS notification delivery.
